name: Catalan (Valencian)
variety: Valencian (Western dialect group): general Valencian as codified by the Acadèmia Valenciana de la Llengua, with notes on the central (apitxat) and southern areas
sources: Carbonell, Joan F. and Llisterri, Joaquim (1992). Catalan. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 22(1-2), 53-56. Reprinted in the Handbook of the International Phonetic Association (1999), Cambridge University Press.
Wheeler, Max W. (2005). The Phonology of Catalan. Oxford University Press.
Recasens, Daniel (1996). Fonètica descriptiva del català. 2nd edition. Barcelona: Institut d'Estudis Catalans.
Veny, Joan (1982). Els parlars catalans: síntesi de dialectologia. Palma: Moll.
Acadèmia Valenciana de la Llengua (2006). Gramàtica normativa valenciana. València: Acadèmia Valenciana de la Llengua.
Saborit Vilar, Josep (2009). Millorem la pronúncia. València: Acadèmia Valenciana de la Llengua.

Recasens, Daniel and Espinosa, Aina (2005). Articulatory, positional and coarticulatory characteristics for clear /l/ and dark /l/: evidence from two Catalan dialects. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 35(1), 1-25.
Recasens, Daniel and Espinosa, Aina (2006). Dispersion and variability of Catalan vowels. Speech Communication 48, 645-666.

Recasens, Daniel and Espinosa, Aina (2007). An electropalatographic and acoustic study of affricates and fricatives in two Catalan dialects. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 37(2), 143-172.
Prieto, Pilar et al. (2015). Intonational phonology of Catalan and its dialectal varieties. In Frota and Prieto (eds.), Intonation in Romance. Oxford University Press.
contrasts: seven vowels under stress /i e ɛ a ɔ o u/ and five in unstressed syllables [i e a o u]; there is no schwa and no reduction of a, e to [ə] or of o to [u]
close-mid versus open-mid vowels under stress, with very open /ɛ ɔ/; many words with Central [ɛ] have [e] (cadena [kaˈðena], francés [fɾanˈses])
/v/ is distinct from /b/ in general Valencian (merged in the central apitxat area)
voiced affricate /dʒ/ for written j and g before e, i in all positions (roja [ˈrɔdʒa], gent [dʒent]); there is no phoneme /ʒ/
/s/ versus /z/ between vowels (devoiced in the apitxat area)
obstruent voicing is neutralised at the end of a word
allophony: unstressed vowels keep their quality; open-mid vowels merge with close-mid ones when unstressed

vowel harmony in southern and some central areas: final unstressed -a copies a stressed open-mid vowel of the preceding syllable (terra [ˈtɛrɛ], dona [ˈdɔnɔ]); it is regional and not part of the formal standard
initial unstressed e before s, n, m is lowered to [a] in everyday speech (escola, entendre); descriptions treat this as colloquial next to [e]
word-final r is pronounced: cantar [kanˈtaɾ], flor [flɔɾ], primer [pɾiˈmeɾ]
final clusters keep their stop: pont [pɔnt], camp [kamp], alt [alt], molt [molt]
written x is [tʃ] at the start of most words (xiquet [tʃiˈket]) and [ʃ] in others and after i (Xàtiva, caixa [ˈkajʃa], peix [pejʃ]); the glide of the spelling ix is pronounced
/l/ is clearer (less velarised) than in the eastern dialects (Recasens and Espinosa 2005)
/b d ɡ/ are approximants [β ð ɣ] after vowels and continuants; the d of -ada, -ador is commonly dropped in everyday speech (vesprada [vesˈpɾaː])
word-final obstruents are voiceless before pause and assimilate in voicing to a following consonant
apitxat (central Valencian): /z/ and /dʒ/ are devoiced to [s] and [tʃ], and /v/ merges with /b/
phonotactics: word-final clusters of sonorant plus stop are pronounced in full
/ɾ/ does not begin a word but occurs word-finally; /ʎ/ and /ɲ/ occur in all positions
geminates of the spelling (tl, tm, l·l) are generally simplified

stress.type: lexical, on one of the last three syllables
stress.rule: Words ending in a vowel, a vowel plus s, or -en, -in are stressed on the penultimate syllable, other words on the last; all exceptions carry a written accent.
stress.cues: duration and pitch; vowel quality plays a smaller part than in Eastern Catalan because unstressed vowels are not reduced

rhythm.vowel_reduction: none as a system: unstressed syllables have the five vowels [i e a o u]
rhythm.notes: No rhythm measurements specific to Valencian are cited here; the published Catalan figures are for other speakers.

length.notes: No length contrast. A long [aː] arises in everyday speech from -ada after loss of the d.

intonation.declarative: rising accents with a delayed peak before the nucleus, low nuclear accent on the last stressed syllable and low boundary
intonation.yes_no_question: mostly rising: low on the last stressed syllable, then a rise to a high boundary
intonation.wh_question: high on the question word, falling to a low boundary
intonation.continuation: rising accent with high boundary at the end of non-final phrases
intonation.accent_shape: prenuclear L+<H* with the peak after the stressed syllable; nuclear L* in statements
intonation.notes: Prieto et al. (2015) cover Valencian within their survey of Catalan varieties; detail differs between northern, central and southern Valencian.

problems: no tune set is selected, so the generic default tunes are used
initial unstressed e before s, n, m is always lowered to [a] (escola [askˈɔla], estar [astˈaɾ], entendre [antˈendɾe]), which is the colloquial variant; careful speech has [e]
/l/ is inherited from the Central table (English phoneme with dark coda l), although Valencian /l/ is the clearest of the Catalan dialects
què and perquè are given close [e] ([kˈe], [peɾkˈe]); Valencian keeps open [ɛ] in these words, which is why they are written with a grave accent also in Valencian spelling
no option for the regional features: vowel harmony of final -a, loss of d in -ada, or the devoicing and b/v merger of the apitxat area
good: no reduction to schwa and no raising of unstressed o: five unstressed vowels as in the dialect
final r is pronounced (cantar [kantˈaɾ]) and final clusters keep their stop (pont [pˈɔnt], camp [kˈamp])
written j, g are the affricate [dʒ] in all positions (roja [rˈɔdʒa], llegir [ʎedʒˈiɾ]) and initial x is [tʃ]
no gemination in poble and setmana; -itzar has [z]; Western close [e] in cadena, francés

notes: The voice combines rule sets 2 and 3 of ca_rules with its own phoneme table. Valencian spelling uses the acute accent in words such as francés, café where the general Catalan norm writes è.
